entries.title: Choose a clear side for rim contact
fields: For an open vessel crowded by its handle or neighboring objects, choose a clear rim side and engage the wall below the observed top. Select the closing and approach directions from that side's visible clearance.
Mugs, cups, bowls, and similar open vessels in surface- or container-placement tasks.

A top-down rim pinch can push or lose an open vessel even when the vessel is correctly localized, especially when its handle or a nearby object crowds the selected rim side. Use the observed upper body and rim extent to choose a side clear of the handle and surrounding clutter. Select the corresponding closing and downward-approach directions, place the contact near that side of the rim, and engage the vertical wall below the observed top. Preserve the grasp-to-body planar relation when placing the vessel.

entries.title: Grasp a long handle near its root
fields: For a long handle whose midpoint contact slips during transport, choose a thicker region near its root. Ground contact height in that local region rather than the whole handle.
Pans, handled cookware, and long handled tools.

A midpoint handle contact can lose the object during horizontal transport. Moving toward the handle root changes the local contact height because that region slopes toward the body. Associate the handle with its parent and infer its direction relative to the body. Select a thicker region toward the root, ground contact height in that local region rather than the whole handle, and adjust engagement in small steps while preserving the image-selected closing and approach directions.

entries.title: Identify the actionable receptacle opening
fields: Distinguish a receptacle's broad opening from an edge or wall patch using visible area, overlap and containment relative to the parent. Leave the opening unresolved when those relationships are ambiguous.
Baskets, bins, drawers, and trays after localizing the semantic parent.
Apply to baskets, bins, drawers, and trays after localizing the semantic parent.

entries.title: Choose a supported interior placement
fields: For an obliquely viewed receptacle, compare its structure with the visible opening before selecting the interior destination. A visible wall alone does not identify the supporting interior.
Object-in-basket and object-in-bin/drawer tasks viewed obliquely.

Failure signature: an open basket/bin/drawer is semantically localized, but a full-mask median aims at a visible wall or an opening-only mask is biased toward the visible back half, so a retained object collides with the rim or lands outside. Use trimmed bounds of the full receptacle structure to center the occluded depth axis, trimmed bounds of an opening/interior mask to center the unobstructed lateral axis, and a dense low interior band for support Z. Preserve the measured grasp-to-object-bottom offset, transport above the rim, descend vertically, release just above the support, retreat vertically when clearance allows, and settle.

entries.title: Continue a partially completed slider stroke
fields: When a slider moves and then stalls, preserve the achieved displacement. Reobserve the same part and continue only the remaining inward stroke, without an outward action that undoes progress.
Resistant prismatic sliders in drawers, appliance trays, and cabinet panels.

Failure signature: a drawer, sliding tray, or panel moves usefully during a retained or closed-finger push, but commanded later waypoints complete while the wrist deflects, the grasp is lost, or the slider stalls short. Open at the achieved endpoint without outward retreat, disengage orthogonally, re-observe and re-localize the shifted part using relative geometry plus continuity, then use fresh short monotonic compact-pusher strokes. Stop rather than act if recovery segmentation merges adjacent repeated handles.

entries.title: Place the support bowl before stacking
fields: When the task allows reordering and carrying a nested pair is unsupported, put the support bowl in the tray first. Preserve that relation, then place the upper bowl on it.
This task requests left-bowl-on-right-bowl and the resulting pair in the tray, while public observations provide no verified way to carry two nested bowls.

Decision change: place the designated right/support bowl in the tray first, publicly verify and preserve that completed relation, then execute only the left-bowl-on-support suffix. Supporting observation: the lower bowl remains visibly contained while the left bowl is acquired and transported. Disconfirming observation: the lower bowl is not contained after its release, moves during the upper-bowl suffix, or the task language/public state requires an intermediate stack before tray placement. Then stop and preserve the scene rather than replaying the prefix.

entries.title: Rebind a support bowl after moving it
fields: After the support bowl moves into the tray, rebind it from current containment evidence. Its former relational description may now identify a different bowl; continue only with an unambiguous support.
After the right bowl has been moved into the tray, two visually similar bowls remain and a relational phrase may rank the untouched bowl above the moved one.

Disconfirming observation: no candidate or multiple candidates plausibly lie in the tray, current tray geometry is unresolved, or the tray already contains another bowl. Then identity is unresolved and the suffix must not continue.

entries.title: Verify placement before closing a drawer
fields: Preserve the place-before-close order for a carton and drawer. Permit closure only after fresh observations support the carton within the intended drawer's footprint and above its floor.
The brown carton has been released near the bound open upper drawer and drawer closure is still unexecuted.

Decision change: preserve the place-before-close order and issue the closing interaction only when a fresh public observation supports the requested carton above the measured drawer floor and within the originally observed drawer footprint. Otherwise stop and preserve the released state. A post-close handle mask that jumps to another cabinet is not grounds for another push. Disconfirming observation: a continuity-valid carton mask outside the drawer or an unresolved destination prevents closure.

entries.title: Maintain contact through a wiping sweep
fields: For a wiping sweep, maintain surface contact through short Cartesian segments, including transitions between rows. Inspect the first row's physical effect before extending coverage.
Spill wiping and other sustained surface-contact sweeps.
Verify the first row's physical effect before tuning coverage.

entries.title: Verify both contacts before a bimanual lift
fields: When both hands close on opposed handles but the object stays on its support, seat the contacts toward the handle-to-handle axis before beginning a short synchronized lift.
Bimanual handled containers and tray/frame lifts.

Failure signature: both arms reach and close on opposed handles, but the first vertical lift leaves the object on its support. Repair: preserve the observation-derived closing/approach axes, close both grippers, then move both hands a small equal distance inward along the handle-to-handle axis to seat the crossbars against the outer fingers before beginning with a short synchronized lift.

entries.title: Acquire a tall tapered bottle
fields: When a tapered upright container is disturbed by a low approach, preserve the selected side and move the contact toward its upper body, above the unstable taper.
Tapered condiment bottles, jars, and similar upright packages in both container-placement and surface-placement tasks.
From the public object mask, estimate XY using the midpoint of robust bounds of an extreme-top slice.

entries.title: Acquire a tapered bottle below its cap
fields: For a tapered bottle with an accessible side corridor, approach the upper body horizontally rather than repeating an ineffective downward contact near the cap.
Public RGB/depth shows a clear horizontal approach corridor.
Apply when public RGB/depth shows a clear horizontal approach corridor.

entries.title: Acquire an upright carton
fields: For an upright rectangular package, select the narrow pair of opposing side faces and a body contact between its visible top and bottom. Align the closing direction with those faces.
Cartons and compact boxes in both object-in-container and object-on-surface tasks.
Apply to cartons and compact boxes in both object-in-container and object-on-surface tasks.

entries.title: Acquire an upright cylindrical package
fields: For an upright cylindrical package, choose a body-centered contact and explicit closing and downward approach directions from the current view.
Cans, jars, bottles, and similar upright objects in container or surface placement.
Failure signature: an upright cylindrical package is correctly segmented but needs a reproducible non-generated grasp.

entries.title: Activate the stove before placing the pan
fields: Activate the stove before moving the pan when its control is exposed. Preserve the visibly active state during the transition to the pan and check it again before placing the pan.
The task requires stove activation before moving a pan.

For this task, when public RGB shows the pan off an inactive stove and the raised stove control is exposed, activate the stove before moving the pan. After each bounded control increment, inspect fresh RGB inside the localized burner mask and stop as soon as the red active appearance is present and persists. Then release, retreat, route the open hand through the documented home pose, and proceed to the pan only if fresh observations still show activation after home and at the high pan pregrasp. This changes the progress and transition-route decisions: it avoids both continuing past a completed activation and crossing directly through the control workspace. The method is called into question if the control does not visibly co-move on the first rotation, the red appearance never emerges or does not persist, or home routing changes the state.

entries.title: Adapt rim contact to handle clearance
fields: For a handled vessel, choose the rim side with enough room for the fingers and the following lift. Engage the side wall while keeping the handle outside the approach corridor.
Mugs, cups, small pots, and similar handled vessels in both surface-placement and container-placement tasks.

Segment the semantic parent, a parent-qualified handle, and the rim. Compute the robust rim/body center and handle center. Contact near one robust rim radius on that side and roughly 12-20 mm below the rim top.

entries.title: Advance only on observed physical progress
fields: For butter-to-tray placement, advance from acquisition to transport only on observed object motion. After release, judge the remaining goal from the package's settled relation to the intended tray.

After the shortest probe, continue only if the requested red/yellow carton is elevated/co-moving and no comparable low instance remains at its source. After the single release and bounded settling observations, stop only if the qualified carton center is inside the initially perceived trimmed tray bounds, low relative to the rim, and away from source. Unresolved perception reports uncertainty without replaying completed actions. A low source instance, wrong item motion, elevated/attached final carton, out-of-tray center, or unresolved view calls the decision into question.

entries.title: Align a held body with its target
fields: For a ring or handled object, distinguish the acquired contact from the feature that must meet the target. Placement should align the opening or body with its destination.
For a ring or handled object.

Failure signature: transport visibly succeeds, but release places the object beside the target because the robot was commanded to put its off-center grasp point at the target. Apply whenever grasp point and functional placement feature differ, such as a handled ring onto a peg or a mug held by its handle onto a locator. Repair: before grasping, localize and deproject both the grasp point and functional feature at a common object-surface depth.

entries.title: Approach without sweeping through clutter
fields: When clutter obstructs a low approach, first reach a clear position above the selected object, then descend through the visible corridor while preserving the chosen contact directions.
Cluttered vessel, grocery-package, or tool pickup.
Apply in cluttered vessel, grocery-package, or tool pickup.

entries.title: Assess drawer placement after release
fields: After releasing an object near a drawer, inspect its relation to the intended interior before marking placement complete. Keep an unresolved destination relation open.
After releasing an object near a drawer.

Trigger: a fresh public view shows the black bowl already supported within the selected drawer even though the cleanup/release suffix has not completed normally. Decision change: recognize the requested relation as completed, preserve the placed bowl and stop instead of replaying pickup or transport. Treat the late exception as a failed or unnecessary suffix rather than loss of all progress. This rule is called into question when the bowl is outside the drawer, unstable, or still moving with the hand.

entries.title: Associate a part with its parent object
fields: Bind an actionable part to its visible parent before using it. Require the part's position and extent to agree with the parent's geometry.
Handled cookware, mugs, tools, and appliance parts in clutter.

Accept only candidates with a plausible parent-relative direction, distance, and cross-axis alignment. Estimate contact height from a dense interior/lower band after rejecting tall clusters. Use the part for the along-axis coordinate and regularize the cross-axis coordinate from the parent while estimating the local handle yaw.

entries.title: Balance rim engagement and release clearance
fields: Choose rim engagement with both pickup and release in mind. A contact that retains the vessel can still leave an inner finger trapped when the vessel reaches its support.
Mugs/cups and handled tools or cookware with a vertical loop.

Failure signature: repeated rim grasps on a handled vessel alternate between narrow tip retention that slips on short lift and deep wide jams that tilt the vessel, while a distinct handle is publicly visible. Segment the semantic parent and a parent-qualified handle. Select a robust outer mid-height handle band. Choose an explicit world-frame jaw axis normal to the observed handle plane and world-down approach. Because monocular public depth measures the camera-facing handle surface, center the thin handle by shifting a small geometry-scaled amount toward its occluded half along the same jaw line.

entries.title: Bind a black bowl and its plate
fields: Bind the requested black bowl and its plate as separate scene entities. Require each selected region to match the instruction and the current visible geometry.
The task names a black bowl and a plate that require separate bindings.

Continue only when those masks are geometrically consistent with the visible roles. Multiple compact black vessels, multiple plates, an invalid mask shape, sparse depth, or role ambiguity would call the binding into question and require fresh disambiguation.

entries.title: Bind a bowl among background distractors
fields: For bowl-to-cabinet placement, distinguish the compact black vessel from background cabinetry and identify the foreground cabinet's supporting top.

When this task's public instruction requests the black bowl and the scene also contains background cabinetry, bind the source by trying 'black ceramic bowl', then 'black bowl' and 'bowl', retaining a compact bowl-shaped mask, and bind the destination with 'cabinet top surface', then parent-qualified top-surface fallbacks, retaining a broad horizontal public-depth plane. The trigger is ambiguity between the small task cabinet and background cabinets. Supporting observations are a compact mask at the black open vessel plus a broad high plane on the small cabinet. This rule is called into question by multiple compact black bowls, no geometry-valid top mask, or a top too small for the bowl.

entries.title: Bind a middle bowl using distinct instances
fields: When exactly three distinct black bowls have an unambiguous image-row order, bind the middle instance by that relative order. Do not apply the rule when the count, viewpoint or separation is unresolved.
When exactly three distinct black bowls have an unambiguous image-row order.

Disconfirming observation: fewer/more than three plausible instances, changed viewpoint/order, or another instance moving under the diagnostic lift makes the rule inapplicable and should stop rather than guess.

entries.title: Bind a thin package to a frozen grasp option
fields: Bind a thin package to a frozen local grasp option whose contact surfaces are visible and accessible. Keep the task referent fixed while selecting the applicable local skill.
A thin package is bound for pickup and several local contact options remain possible.

Trigger: correct-identity before/after public images show that push signature, not merely a low aperture. Decision change: in a fresh episode, bind the same center, contact depth, world-down approach, destination, and ordering to the frozen thin-package opposite-jaw-sign alternative.

entries.title: Bind alphabet soup and its basket
fields: Distinguish the alphabet-soup can from other groceries, then bind the intended basket's interior as the destination rather than its exterior wall.
The task asks for alphabet soup in a basket among several visible groceries.

Several grocery containers may be visible beside the basket. Bind the requested soup can using its visible appearance and compact upright shape. Bind a broad basket interior to its visible parent; a small edge or exterior patch does not establish the destination.

entries.title: Bind an open drawer's interaction
fields: For closing an open drawer, select the frozen inward-push capability instead of a pull objective. Preserve a drawer that is already closed and assess progress from the same drawer's observed displacement.
The requested top drawer is visibly open, the same parent-qualified handle is reachable, and the visible path from the handle toward its cabinet is clear.

Decision change: bind the remaining goal to the frozen direct-push capability rather than grasp/pull. Order localization before the inward effect, release at the achieved endpoint without an outward retreat that could reverse closure, and judge progress from re-observed motion and retained closure of the same drawer rather than command completion. If already closed, preserve it and do not act. Disconfirming observations: a different part moves, the intended handle moves away from the cabinet, no target motion follows aligned contact, the drawer rebounds after release, or the path is obstructed. Exact contact and motion mechanics remain frozen Cerebellum concerns.

entries.title: Bind basket interior relative to its parent
fields: Bind a basket's actionable interior to its parent container. An unrelated small region or exterior patch does not establish an interior destination.
A basket is visible but its actionable interior is not yet bound.

Proceed only when the interior mask is a broad, centered, parent-consistent region rather than a tiny rim patch. Use the parent and interior together as the destination input to the frozen basket-placement procedure. Reject or leave unresolved when the interior candidate is tiny, outside the parent, or lacks adequate public depth.

entries.title: Bind cream cheese and its tray
fields: For cream-cheese placement, bind the compact requested package separately from the larger wooden tray and its interior. Keep the task unresolved if the package identity or parent-interior relationship is ambiguous.

Require relative image geometry in which the tray is substantially larger than the package and the interior occupies a meaningful part of the tray before moving. Supporting observations are a compact task-qualified target mask with coherent public depth and a broad nested tray/interior pair.

entries.title: Bind ketchup and the wooden tray
fields: Identify the ketchup bottle among groceries and bind the wooden tray's interior before composing pickup and placement.
A ketchup bottle and a wooden tray must be identified among grocery distractors.
A can/carton match, tiny tray-edge patch, sparse depth, or non-broad interior mask disconfirms applicability and should stop or trigger re-observation.

entries.title: Bind placement to the rim-held bowl's body
fields: For a rim-held bowl, retain the bowl body's relation to the plate as the placement objective. Do not substitute the hand's arrival for that object-level relation.

For this black-bowl-on-plate task, when the applicable frozen procedure uses an asymmetric rim contact, bind placement to the bowl body rather than centering the wrist: measure the public pre-pick vector from bowl-body XY to grasp XY and command destination wrist XY as plate-center XY plus that vector. Supporting observations are that the requested bowl is retained after lift and the final bowl center remains over the plate. Disconfirming observations are bowl rotation/slip that changes the held-body offset, failed co-motion, or an unresolved plate center, in which case this pre-pick offset must not authorize descent.

entries.title: Bind the book and the requested caddy compartment
fields: Bind the requested book and the requested caddy compartment separately. The entire caddy does not resolve which interior compartment the instruction requires.
The task names a book and a particular caddy compartment.

Accept only masks whose public image/depth geometry is consistent with one tall upright book and one full-height caddy compartment. A missing mask, a generic multi-compartment union, implausible tall-object extent, or multiple unresolved instances calls the binding into question and must stop motion.

entries.title: Bind the foreground cabinet's top drawer
fields: For opening the foreground cabinet's top drawer, bind the handle to that cabinet before choosing the opening objective. Keep repeated background handles separate from the intended drawer.
For opening the foreground cabinet's top drawer.

Reject high horizontal candidates associated with background cabinetry. From the current handle-to-parent face geometry, choose the outward drawer direction and order handle acquisition before monotonic opening motion. Supporting observations are selection of the foreground top handle and first-pull co-motion of that drawer with the gripper. A high/horizontal selection, invalid depth, inward motion, motion of another part, or absent first-pull co-motion calls the method into question.

entries.title: Bind the pan body and cabinet-top destination
fields: For pan placement on a cabinet, bind the pan body as the object to place and the cabinet's supporting top as the destination, while the local skill chooses the handle contact.
For pan placement on a cabinet.

When the public instruction is to put the frying pan on top of the cabinet and RGB-D shows a graspable handle offset from the pan body plus multiple cabinet-like background surfaces, do not bind one centroid to both acquisition and placement. Command the target wrist XY as the robust cabinet-top center plus the freshly measured handle-contact minus pan-body offset. Public support is distinct geometry for all three masks, a planar destination large enough for the body, visible source separation/co-motion after lift, and stable post-release support.

entries.title: Bind visible package faces to a grasp axis
fields: For the thin pudding package in the observed orientation, bind the frozen grasp to its visible opposing faces and clear downward approach. A rotated package or obstructed faces invalidate that binding.
For the thin pudding package in the observed orientation.
A rotated package, obstructed opposing faces, a materially displaced pre-close mask, or failure of the short-lift elevation check disconfirms applicability.

entries.title: Carry a rim-held vessel in short segments
fields: For a vessel held at its rim or handle, divide a long loaded translation into short segments. Reobserve the carried body above the destination before the descent.
Long pick-and-place transports for rim-, handle-, or edge-held objects.

Failure signature: a narrow rim grasp survives lift but slips during one long horizontal move, or the wrist reaches the target while the asymmetrically held object is off-center. Move at constant safe height through short interpolated waypoints (about 5 cm), then reobserve at the high target waypoint. Estimate the held object's actionable body center from a robust top slice, compute target minus held-object XY, reject implausible residuals, and apply conservative proportional corrections with remeasurement.

entries.title: Center an asymmetrically held object
fields: When an object is held asymmetrically, use the body's observed relation to the destination to judge alignment. Reaching the destination with the hand does not establish body alignment.
Books/cards into caddies and also edge-held trays, packages, or tools entering bins, shelves, and holders.

Failure signature: an asymmetrically or edge-grasped object remains retained and the wrist reaches the nominal target, but final descent contacts an adjacent wall or the object lands across neighboring compartments because the held body is offset from the wrist. Apply delta to the high wrist pose, descend vertically, and use contact-aware release/settling. Bound delta at the scale of the full transport, not a local correction.

entries.title: Check realized clearance during lift
fields: When a larger lift causes a lateral excursion, preserve the completed lift and replace only the failed suffix with shorter monotonic upward moves.
When a larger lift causes a lateral excursion.

The object remains with the hand through early lifting, but a larger final upward move sends the hand sideways. Preserve the height already reached and replace only the failed suffix with shorter monotonic upward moves. Stop before a discontinuous motion and use a lower transit height when the scene still provides sufficient clearance.

entries.title: Check realized pose before continuing
fields: Before a low contact, stage above the selected location and descend through short local steps. Check the realized hand pose before closing.
Low tabletop pickups and low articulated contacts.
Verify realized pose or contact before closing.

entries.title: Check retention before a long basket transfer
fields: Before a long basket transfer, establish that the requested object has been acquired. Keep the remaining transport objective pending when retention is unresolved.

Require public named-box co-motion: the compact box geometry must rise from its prior support and remain hand-associated. If the box stays at the source, another item moves, or all public views are inconclusive, halt and preserve the reached state without replaying acquisition.

entries.title: Check stacking progress from the current scene
fields: After a bowl has reached its support bowl, preserve the completed pickup and carry. Gate only the remaining descent and release on fresh evidence that the same bowl is still elevated at the destination.
After a bowl has reached its support bowl.

Continue only when the elevated source remains with the tool over the destination, otherwise stop without repicking. Supporting observation: a plausible elevated bowl mask near the tool and above the destination. Disconfirming observation: the source is resting, separated, associated with the wrong destination, or too occluded to decide.

entries.title: Check the first lift before loaded transport
fields: For the selected red mug, check the first lift's observed elevation before authorizing the remaining transport. Keep the destination undisturbed while resolving acquisition.

For this task, after one close and the first short lift of the selected red mug, do not authorize the remaining lift and transport from command completion or gripper aperture alone. A mug remaining on its support, separating from the hand, an unresolved/inconsistent mask, or destination motion disconfirms progress and requires preserving the actual scene and stopping before long transport.

entries.title: Choose the grasp input from local clearance
fields: Bind the selected soup can to the local grasp option that fits its present approach clearance. Preserve the object and destination bindings when choosing that option.
A selected soup can has limited approach clearance near neighboring objects.
Stop before motion when bilateral clearance is not visible.

entries.title: Clear a raised receptacle during transport
fields: For a raised receptacle, establish clearance for the held object's lowest extent before moving across the rim. Observe the high destination alignment before beginning a vertical descent.
Object-in-basket/bin placement and placement over raised fixtures.

Failure signature: a nominal high waypoint silently produces no useful motion, or the wrist arrives high while the held object's bottom clips and displaces a raised target. Split transport into an intermediate high waypoint and a high target waypoint. Once centered with clearance, descend vertically, release, and retreat vertically. This prevents the next low command from becoming a diagonal collision after a failed high move.

entries.title: Clear the inner finger after release
fields: After releasing a rim-held vessel, an inner finger may still hook the rim. Establish support and clear the engaged finger toward the visible exterior before lifting it away.
Rim-held vessels placed on surfaces or into containers.

Failure signature: after opening a one-finger-inside/one-outside rim grasp, the inside finger remains in the vessel. Vertical retreat hooks the rim and lifts the object back off the target, while staying still leaves it mechanically supported by the robot. Seat the vessel before opening, then extract at contact height toward the exterior side of the selected rim before any upward retreat, and settle only after the finger is clear.

entries.title: Close a hinged panel along its arc
fields: For a hinged panel, distinguish the closing direction from the opening direction using the panel's observed response. Follow the visible hinge arc with local contacts and preserve the achieved closure.
Microwave, oven, cabinet, and similar hinged doors.

After lowering, a first displacement may instead increase the opening angle. Preserve observed XY and explicit tool axes, lower contact in measured increments until the pads visibly overlap the panel, then use a small diagnostic displacement to identify the closing tangent.

entries.title: Close a slider with compact pushes
fields: For monotonic slider closure, a compact closed-finger contact can move the panel without acquiring its handle. Preserve useful displacement when a stroke stops short.
Closing drawers, sliding trays, and prismatic cabinet panels when the goal direction is a monotonic push.
Repair: keep the last collision-free public-depth surface pose. Close the fingers there to form a compact rigid pusher rather than requiring retention.

entries.title: Compensate an off-center grasp
fields: When the contact is away from an object's center, judge placement using the carried body and the intended support rather than the hand alone.
Pans and other handled vessels, edge-grasped trays, and tools.

Failure signature: an asymmetrically grasped object's wrist reaches the target while its functional body remains offset, or the direct compensated wrist pose is near the workspace limit. Before pickup, estimate grasp-point and body centers from public depth. Set release Z by preserving the measured contact-to-bottom height above the target top. Verify retention after lift before rotating or transporting.

entries.title: Confirm acquisition before lifting
fields: For a small rigid object, inspect where the finger pads meet its side faces. Correct an above-body or below-body contact before extending the lift and transport.
Top-down grasps of small rigid objects in stacking, sorting, or pick-and-place.

Repair: inspect the close image for the actual dark contact pads. If they end above or below the object's side faces, adjust the hand target incrementally along the explicit observed approach axis. Otherwise stop or recover the failed suffix.

entries.title: Confirm mug retention from current evidence
fields: Use current evidence to decide whether the requested mug remains acquired before continuing its task. Do not advance the task merely because a hand command completed.
A mug contact has occurred but continued retention is unresolved.

Decision change: execute only the first short planned lift, re-segment the same task-qualified mug, and authorize the remaining transport only when public depth shows a plausible upward median-Z change with limited planar drift. After the single release and full clearance, re-segment again and require the mug center inside the initially selected right-plate bounds with its bottom near support. Preserve the actual scene and stop without replaying the completed prefix when either gate fails. Disconfirming observations: the target remains on its old support, fails to track the first lift, shifts too far in XY, changes semantic identity, or finishes outside the selected plate bounds.

entries.title: Contact the body of a short cylinder
fields: For a short cylinder, select opposing body surfaces rather than a contact above the lid. Ground the approach in the object's visible body geometry.
Cans, jars, short bottles, and cylindrical cartons in container- or surface-placement tasks.
Estimate XY from a robust extreme-top slice and body contact height from a middle public-depth band.

entries.title: Disambiguate a butter package
fields: Distinguish the requested butter package from similarly shaped groceries using its visible appearance and task context before binding pickup.
A butter package appears among similarly shaped groceries.

Refuse action if another candidate is close in score. Apply the existing acquisition only after that distinction, then continue to carry only if a small probe lift produces fresh public RGB-D evidence that the requested carton is elevated/co-moving and absent from its source.

entries.title: Disengage from a close-fitting receptacle
fields: In a close-fitting receptacle, plan how the open fingers can leave the object without catching its rim or the surrounding walls. Preserve the placed object's support during disengagement.
Books/cards entering caddies or bins and tools/utensils entering holders.

Failure signature: a narrow object is retained and the wrist reaches a close-fitting receptacle, but opening deflects the object against the walls or leaves it wedged because the initial commanded grasp-to-bottom offset differs from the achieved held-body offset.

entries.title: Distinguish a milk carton from distractors
fields: Bind the requested milk carton by its package appearance and shape. Reject a different grocery item even when it occupies a convenient contact location.
The requested milk carton appears among other grocery items.
Multiple eligible milk masks, a non-upright mask, sparse depth, or disagreement with the visible label calls the binding into question and should stop motion.

entries.title: Distinguish a stove knob from cookware parts
fields: For a stove-control task, bind the stove's raised control separately from cookware handles and other nearby parts.
Disconfirming observation: no substantial burner-associated candidate, multiple equally plausible appliance controls, or incoherent RGB-D geometry should leave the referent unresolved.

entries.title: Distinguish basket facade from opening
fields: Distinguish a basket's exterior facade from the opening used for placement. Keep the destination tied to the supporting interior.
The basket facade can be confused with its placement opening.

Keep the interior as a separate opening role. The public trigger is competing parent masks with materially different extent. Support is the larger mask enclosing the broad opening and body, while lack of parent-interior overlap, implausible image scale, or no visible boundary calls the decision into question and requires stopping.

entries.title: Distinguish support contact from free motion
fields: Distinguish the intended final support contact from free-space motion. Observe whether the object has reached its support before deciding how to release it.
Object-on-shelf/surface placement and shallow container seating.

Failure signature: all free-space transport waypoints realize correctly and the object visibly reaches its support, but the final lowering pose deviates under intended contact and a generic pose checker aborts before release. Keep strict realized-pose checks for collision-clear motion.

entries.title: Distinguish the moka pot from similar objects
fields: Identify the requested moka pot as a complete task entity before binding its actionable part. Do not substitute another dark or metallic kitchen object.
A moka pot must be distinguished from other dark or metallic kitchen objects.

Bind 'stove' to a geometry-valid circular support from 'stove burner' or 'burner', rather than an arbitrary appliance/counter patch. Call the method into question if no compact candidate exists, public depth is inconsistent with an upright moka, or no bounded burner support is observed.

entries.title: Distinguish the requested white mug
fields: Use the requested white mug's visible appearance and vessel geometry to distinguish it from other cups or background regions.
A requested white mug must be distinguished from other cups or background regions.

Disconfirming observations: do not apply this method when no geometry-valid qualified body/handle pair exists, the selected body does not co-move on the first lift, the plate is unresolved, or the final mug base is visibly outside the plate.

entries.title: Engage the sides of a thin object
fields: For a thin object, position the opposing pads against its side surfaces. Contact on or above the top face alone may push the object without acquiring it.
Flat boxes, packets, cards, and similarly low objects in pick-to-container or pick-to-surface tasks.
Keep the observed center, depth, and downward approach fixed.

entries.title: Establish contact before rotating
fields: Establish a contact that visibly engages the rotary control before attempting its turn. Motion of the hand alone does not establish motion of the control.
Knobs and other small tabletop controls where nominal TCP offsets do not yield contact.

Preserve XY and explicit observed tool axes, change only the requested contact height in measured increments, and verify physical effect in images. If the visual goal is already achieved, gate or omit later waypoints because over-rotation or slip can undo success.

entries.title: Gate traversal on the first lift's evidence
fields: At the pickup-to-transport boundary, require supported acquisition of the requested source before beginning a long traversal. Keep the remaining task pending when the first lift is unresolved.

Reobserve with public RGB-D and continue only when the same qualified red-mug mask has materially risen from its prior support while remaining within a bounded planar association to the pickup line. If it stays behind, changes identity, or cannot be associated confidently, stop and preserve the actual scene without repeating the grasp.

entries.title: Grasp a thin tabletop package
fields: For a thin tabletop package, choose visible opposing edges with enough access for the finger pads. Keep the approach aligned with those edges.

From public depth, take a robust top height and robust XY-bound midpoint. Select explicit observed world-frame jaw and downward approach axes. Lower contact in measured increments until the pads overlap the object sides.

entries.title: Grasp the material around an open ring
fields: For an open ring, acquire the visible material surrounding the opening. Keep the ring's aperture distinct from the solid contact region.
Nuts, rings with handles, keyed washers, and other apertured parts with a solid protrusion.

Failure signature: a gripper closes over a ring-shaped object's mask centroid and the post-lift image shows the object unmoved, because the centroid is an empty aperture. Or it reaches a tab but closes along the tab length. Do not use PCA or a grasp generator.

entries.title: Grasp with nearby clutter
fields: In clutter, choose a contact whose opening, approach and lift corridors remain clear of neighboring objects. Preserve the selected object identity through contact.
Cans, jars, cartons, tools, and other objects in tight clutter.

Failure signature: SAM and depth give the correct compact-object center, but the final open-finger descent displaces a neighboring package, the realized low pose deflects, and closure reaches the air value.

entries.title: Ground contact in visible body geometry
fields: Ground the contact in the observed body of the requested object. Keep the chosen contact direction tied to visible surfaces rather than an unexamined nominal center.
A fixed camera sees mainly one face of an opaque pot, bottle, box, or similar volume and the grasp center was derived from visible mask points.

Preserve the chosen explicit jaw and approach axes, height, and later trajectory. Along the jaw axis, measure robust visible bounds and shift the center toward the occluded half by a bounded fraction of the visible span.

entries.title: Identify pudding among branded packages
fields: Distinguish the requested pudding package among branded groceries using the visible package identity and geometry, before selecting its local manipulation skill.
A requested pudding package appears among branded grocery distractors.
Continue only when the package mask is compact, the plate mask is materially broader, and both have coherent public depth.

entries.title: Identify the alphabet-soup can
fields: Identify the alphabet-soup can using the instruction and visible label-bearing package. Keep other soup cans and bottles as separate candidates.
Several cans or bottles could be mistaken for the requested alphabet soup.

Several compact upright cans can match the requested soup category. The selected can must also agree with the visible color and label-bearing appearance. If the candidate is absent, duplicated, or hidden by foreground clutter, leave the referent unresolved before pickup.

entries.title: Identify the back bowl by current image order
fields: Use the stable camera's relative image order to identify the back bowl among visibly similar bowls. Apply the relation only while the current viewpoint supports that ordering.
The instruction asks for the black bowl at the back while several visually similar black bowls and one plate are visible from the task's stable public camera.

Decision change: enumerate generic 'black bowl' masks, reject thin, flat, or duplicate detections using public image/depth geometry, order the remaining full bowl instances by camera-relative tabletop depth, choose the farthest as the referent, and bind the sole geometry-valid 'plate' detection as destination. Disconfirming observations: a changed viewpoint, a missing/occluded bowl candidate, a geometry-valid distractor farther from the camera, or post-lift motion of a different object invalidates the decision.

entries.title: Identify the chocolate-pudding package
fields: Bind the requested chocolate-pudding package using its visible appearance and thin package geometry before composing pickup and placement.
A chocolate-pudding package and tray must be bound before pickup.
This changes the decision from generic object/category selection to task-noun-first binding.

entries.title: Identify the front bowl by current image order
fields: For the front bowl, use the bowls' current relative image positions. Reconsider the binding after a viewpoint change, occlusion or object movement.

The decision is called into question if candidate boxes are not comparable, the closest bowl is not greatest-row under the current public camera, or no geometry-valid instance exists. Evidence is program-level and does not isolate this decision causally.

entries.title: Identify the left bowl among similar bowls
fields: Among distinct plausible bowls, bind the image-left instance when the instruction asks for the left bowl. Leave the binding unresolved when occlusion or the view prevents a reliable ordering.
At least two plausible bowl detections are visible in the current public agent view.
Call the method into question when occlusion, a changed view, or candidate geometry prevents a reliable relative image order.

entries.title: Identify the requested red mug
fields: Bind the red mug and the appearance-qualified plate requested by the task. Associate any selected mug handle or rim with that same mug.
The task qualifies both a red mug and its target plate by appearance.
Use parent-qualified 'red mug handle' and 'rim of red mug' only after requiring their image boxes to overlap the selected red-mug parent.

entries.title: Insert and disengage in a narrow cubby
fields: For a thin object entering a narrow cubby, align the body with the opening at a clear height before insertion. Consider how the open fingers will disengage without pulling it back out.
Books or cards entering shelves and thin packages or tools entering low cubbies/close-fitting holders.

Failure signature: a genuinely retained tall thin object reaches a low shelf/cubby entrance but stalls, pivots, or is pulled back out during release/retreat. At collision-clear height, rotate the held object incrementally so its broad face fits the opening.

entries.title: Insert through a shelf entrance
fields: For shelf insertion, stage outside the opening and keep the carried object between the visible support and roof. Separate the inward insertion from the final seating motion.
Pans or trays entering shelves and to books, packages, or tools entering cubbies/holders.

Compute insertion height from the detected shelf plane, grasp-to-object-bottom offset, and a clearance that still fits below the detected roof. Then lower vertically to the seated height. After opening, extract along the grasped part toward the opening before any upward retreat so open fingers do not continue supporting or hook the object.

entries.title: Keep held state provisional until supported
fields: Keep held state provisional after an ambiguous bowl acquisition. Continue transport only when the same bowl visibly rises with the hand and separates from its former support.
A bowl has been contacted but its acquisition is still ambiguous.

For the public situation 'put the black bowl on the plate' when rim closure leaves acquisition ambiguous, keep the held-state decision provisional. After one minimal upward probe, re-identify the task-qualified black bowl in fresh public RGB-D and continue only if it rises with the hand and separates from its former support. Staying behind, separation from the hand, or unresolved re-identification calls the decision into question and stops transport. After observed co-motion supports retention, do not revoke held state solely because aperture drifts slightly across a fixed threshold.

entries.title: Localize a raised control tab
fields: For a raised control on a larger fixture, bind the raised actionable feature separately from its base. The full fixture's visible center may not identify the contact region.
Raised knobs, latches, and handled controls.
Failure signature: a full-object mask centroid is biased by a base or surrounding fixture when the actionable feature is a raised tab.

entries.title: Localize the top of a tall post
fields: For a tall post seen obliquely, distinguish its top from the projected side before choosing the insertion target.
Pegs, posts, bottle necks, and other vertical insertion targets seen obliquely.

Failure signature: a tall post's 2-D box center or full 3-D mask center produces a repeatable millimetric placement bias because the mask includes a projected side face. For apertured source objects, require the expected enclosed-hole topology before accepting a high-scoring candidate.

entries.title: Lower a vessel into a bounded receptacle
fields: When a held vessel tips during the final descent into a bounded receptacle, examine interference with the floor and walls before lowering further. Compare the pre-release and settled object states.
Bowls/cups into trays and irregular objects into bins.

Failure signature: a vessel is upright at a high target waypoint but tips while still held during the final descent into a slatted, raised, or close-fitting container. Preserve target XY and grasp orientation, raise only the release pose until the held object's bottom clears obstructing floor features or walls, open there, omit contact-forcing motions, and allow several stationary observations for gravity settling. Confirm the repair by comparing the last pre-release image with the settled image.

entries.title: Match a two-tone mug to the right plate
fields: Identify the requested two-tone mug and bind the plate on the task-specified right side. Resolve object appearance and the destination relation together.
This task presents three mugs and two similar striped plates under the instruction to put the yellow and white mug on the right plate.

Do not use the ambiguous generic striped-plate result. Disconfirming observations: a qualified part outside the parent-relative region, a degenerate handle-to-rim direction, an ambiguous right-plate mask, or post-lift perception of a different target must reject the binding.

entries.title: Match the red mug to the right plate
fields: Resolve the red-mug qualifier and the right-plate relation before pickup. Multiple plausible mugs or an unresolved plate relation block the dependent action.
The task specifies a red mug and a right-side plate among alternatives.

When this task presents several mugs and two similar plates and the public instruction says to put the red mug on the right plate, change the binding decision from generic category ranking to qualifier-first grounding: query a red-mug-specific description and a right-plate-specific description, require strong geometry-valid masks, and only then bind the frozen pick/place procedures. The supporting public observation is one distinct red-mug mask plus one destination mask consistent with the image-relative right relation.

entries.title: Match the white mug to the left plate
fields: Bind the white mug and the left plate from the current view. Keep the requested appearance and left-right relation distinct from generic object categories.
The instruction specifies a white mug and the left plate.

Supporting observations are a broad mug mask consistent with the separately visible rim/handle and a broad plate mask on the image-left side. Call the method into question if these masks are missing, cross-inconsistent, select another mug, or do not distinguish the left plate.

entries.title: Measure the interior of an open container
fields: For an open container, distinguish the interior support from the rim and visible walls. Use the supporting region that is actually visible inside the container.

Failure signature: an open drawer, bin, or tray is correctly segmented, but using the full-mask point median targets a visible wall or using the mask top causes a high release that bounces the object outside. Apply this to object-in-drawer and object-in-open-container tasks when the semantic mask includes a support floor plus vertical walls. From public depth, isolate the dense lowest plausible horizontal Z band, sanity-check that it contains enough points, compute interior XY as the midpoint of trimmed bounds of that band, and set release height by adding the measured grasp-to-object-bottom offset plus a small clearance to the floor height. Keep transport above the walls and make the final descent vertical.

entries.title: Open a hinged door by handle or pusher
fields: For a hinged door, associate the handle with the correct panel and follow that panel's visible hinge motion. A partial opening alone does not establish the requested fully open state.
Microwaves, ovens, and hinged cabinet doors with a visible handle and vertical hinge.

Segment the semantic parent plus a parent-qualified handle. Estimate the hinge at the robust parent edge opposite the handle. Acquire the handle or close into a compact pusher, then advance the contact around the hinge radius in short monotonic angular waypoints while rotating the jaw axis with the door.

entries.title: Order bottle transport around drawer clearance
fields: After acquiring the upright bottle, inspect the high route over the drawer. When the current orientation already fits, transfer directly instead of inserting an unnecessary reorientation.

After this task's upright bottle is visibly acquired and lifted above the tabletop and drawer rim, inspect the public scene for a clear high translation corridor. If the acquisition orientation already fits that corridor, omit any wrist-roll/reorientation and transfer directly at the unchanged explicit tool axes before descending vertically. The trigger is a retained upright bottle plus a clear high route. The decision changes from an unconditional post-lift roll to direct transport.

entries.title: Orient an elongated object in a shallow tray
fields: For an elongated object in a shallow receptacle, compare its projected length with the available interior. Choose an orientation that keeps both ends within the cavity during release.
Bottles, tools, cartons, and utensils placed in shallow drawers, trays, or bins.

Failure signature: an elongated object is securely transported to a shallow receptacle, but upright release leaves its center above the rim, while a fully horizontal wall-adjacent release deflects or loses it outside. Compare observed object length with floor-to-rim depth. Set release height from floor plus observed radius plus the remaining vertical half-length projection and small relative clearance. Open while both projected endpoints remain within trimmed cavity bounds, allow stationary settling so gravity completes the lay-down, then clear the empty hand.

entries.title: Pinch an open vessel at its rim
fields: For an open vessel, use the solid rim wall as the contact region. Choose an accessible side instead of directing both fingers into the empty interior.
Bowls, cups, and other open vessels whose rim can be pinched.

Failure signature: a vessel is too wide for a full exterior pinch, or a nominal center grasp closes in air. When evidence shows the motion API already realizes the tool/contact offset, command the observed rim contact height directly instead of adding another wrist offset.

entries.title: Place inside an open drawer
fields: When a drawer front hides part of its floor, use the visible drawer structure to distinguish the opening from the front wall. Keep the intended interior and support separate from the handle.
Objects placed in open drawers, deep trays, and bins whose front wall occludes part of the floor.

Use the dense low receptacle band for support Z and the unoccluded lateral coordinate. On the occluded depth axis, center from robust bounds of the full receptacle structure so both back and front are represented. Preserve grasp-minus-body XY, descend vertically until the measured object bottom is just above the floor, open, extract at contact height toward the exterior grasp side, and settle.

entries.title: Place the object body, not the wrist
fields: For a vessel held at its rim or handle, observe the carried body above its support before release. A centered wrist does not guarantee a centered vessel.
Rim, handle, edge, and other asymmetric grasps across vessel-placement and object-in-container tasks.
Failure signature: the hand reaches the target center but an object held off-center lands adjacent to the target, especially when realized wrist yaw changes during transport.

entries.title: Preserve object identity after placement
fields: After package placement, retain the identity of the manipulated object when assessing the final relation. A nearby similar package cannot stand in for the object that was moved.

From one fresh public frame, enumerate geometry-plausible cream-cheese candidates, bind the candidate spatially continuous with the commanded release region, and compare it with a wooden-tray candidate from that same frame. Preserve the released scene and make no recovery motion. Supporting observations are a target-shaped candidate near the release region within the current tray footprint and separation from the open gripper. Disconfirming observations are no plausible nearby candidate, several similar candidates near the tray, or a current tray mask inconsistent with the release. Completion then remains unresolved rather than falling back to score.

entries.title: Preserve progress during slider contact
fields: After partial slider motion, rebind the shifted part using its observed displacement and parent relationship. Continue the unsatisfied closure objective without repeating a completed prefix.

Failure signature: a prismatic drawer, sliding tray, or panel moves usefully during a continuous push but stalls before seating, and an outward disengagement can hook the handle and reverse the achieved motion. Apply this to drawer closing and other monotonic slider-closing tasks. Apply a fresh short monotonic stroke with explicit observed tool axes. At the seated endpoint, open and remain stationary.

entries.title: Reduce visible-side bias in object geometry
fields: For an obliquely viewed flat-topped object, distinguish its top face from visible side faces when selecting the local contact region.
Obliquely viewed cubes, blocks, boxes, and other flat-topped rigid objects.

Failure signature: a full segmentation cloud or 2-D box center is biased by visible side faces, causing a compact object's grasp or placement XY to drift. Estimate object scale from the same robust top-face spans rather than using scene-specific absolute XY.

entries.title: Refresh support height before stacking
fields: After moving the base of a stack, reobserve the base and the new supporting surface before placing the next object. Do not reuse the earlier scene's support height.
Restacking and uniform-block stacking after a preceding contact changes the scene.

Failure signature: a stack placement uses a hard-coded or stale Z and the carried equal-size object collides with the base or releases at the wrong level. Repair: before manipulation, measure the robust vertical center separation of the original equal-size stack. Retract vertically after opening and settle before evaluating. This transfers height from an observed relation rather than a scene-specific absolute coordinate.

entries.title: Reject implausible segmentation patches
fields: Reject a small background patch when its visible shape and extent do not match the requested object. A confident detection alone does not resolve the task referent.
A candidate region may be a background patch rather than the requested object.

Repair: filter all masks for relative image geometry before ranking (for example, sufficient image-relative height, tall aspect ratio, and foreground placement), then choose the highest score among eligible masks and validate its public-depth extent.

entries.title: Release inside a receptacle opening
fields: For an open receptacle, select the interior opening separately from a prominent near wall. Approach the interior from above after clearing the rim.
Baskets, bins, and deep open containers.

Failure signature: using the median of a full open-container mask releases onto a visible near wall, or an object placed below the rim remains supported by the robot. Move to a safe high waypoint, descend centrally below the rim, open, retreat vertically to the high waypoint, then allow settling. Keep the descent vertical after high transport to avoid rim collisions.

entries.title: Release near the interior support
fields: For a rigid object entering a tray or bin, distinguish the interior support from the rim. Releasing above an obstacle can deflect the object away from the intended interior.
Cans/bottles into trays and rigid objects into bins.
Failure signature: a correctly retained rigid object is centered above a raised or slatted open receptacle, but opening above the rim lets it bounce or deflect outside.

entries.title: Release within a close-fitting container
fields: For a close-fitting holder, consider the clearance needed by the opening fingers. Keep release and disengagement from deflecting the object onto the rim.

Failure signature: a narrow object is centered over a close-fitting container, but opening while inserted deflects the hand against the walls, or a later retreat hooks the released object onto the rim. When to apply: books/cards into bins or caddies and narrow tools/utensils into holders. Repair: estimate object bottom and grasp height from public depth, compute the grasp-to-bottom offset, command a release pose that leaves the object bottom slightly above the observed rim while the fingers remain outside, open, omit retreat, and allow stationary settling.

entries.title: Reorient an elongated object for placement
fields: For an elongated object, separate acquisition from placement orientation. Use a clear transport position to reorient the retained body toward the destination's long axis.
Bottles, tools, cartons, or similar elongated objects must move from an easy pickup orientation to a rack, tray, shelf, or horizontal holder.

Repair: infer the support long axis from robust public-depth extents/plane geometry. If needed, first roll the held object about its current long axis in short steps to obtain a jaw axis orthogonal to the desired final approach.

entries.title: Require supported pickup before transport
fields: Keep the pudding package's remaining transport objective pending until the requested package is supported as acquired. Preserve its task identity through the first lift.
The pudding package has been contacted but acquisition remains unresolved.

For this task after the visually selected package approach, do not treat closure or aperture alone as completed pickup. This changes the progress decision from command-completed to perception-supported acquisition. No matched control isolates this gate from the bundled grasp-sign and lift-step changes.

entries.title: Require visual support before basket transport
fields: Before basket transport, use current visual evidence to support acquisition of the requested source. Stop the dependent transport when the object remains at its original support or its identity is unresolved.
On refutation or unresolved re-identification, preserve the actual shifted scene and stop before transport. Call the rule into question when arm occlusion prevents reliable re-identification.

entries.title: Resolve a destination to the right of the caddy
fields: For a destination to the right of the caddy, resolve the relation to the visible parent caddy. Keep that destination separate from the caddy's own compartments.
The instruction says to place the yellow-and-white mug to the right of the caddy, and fresh RGB-D shows the mug starting at a different fore-aft depth or only marginally beyond the caddy edge.
Trigger: robust complete-object masks do not yet show the mug wholly camera-right and fore-aft aligned.

entries.title: Resolve a slatted tray's supported interior
fields: For a slatted tray, bind the supported interior within the parent rather than the lower surface visible through gaps. Keep placement unresolved when no coherent interior is visible.

Decision change: bind the actionable destination region to the coherent dense raised interior band inside the parent and reject the lower gap returns. Stop as unresolved if the inset is not parent-consistent or no coherent band exists. Disconfirming/non-applicability observations: no distinct inset, no coherent raised band, inconsistent parent overlap, heavy occlusion, or a solid-bottom tray where the lowest coherent plane is the real interior.

entries.title: Resolve butter without confidence-only ranking
fields: Use package appearance and geometric plausibility to bind the requested butter. A confident but visually inconsistent region does not establish the task referent.
The requested butter competes with visually similar grocery packages.
The trigger is ambiguity among similarly shaped packages.

entries.title: Resolve foreground versus background cabinet
fields: Resolve whether the instruction refers to foreground furniture or background cabinetry before choosing its actionable surface.
The instruction says cabinet while the RGB view contains both a compact foreground drawer cabinet and background kitchen cabinetry.

Trigger: generic cabinet segmentation ranks broad background cabinets or a non-actionable face. Leave the destination unresolved rather than accepting a tiny patch or background region. Disconfirming observation: the selected mask lies on background cabinetry, is a small edge/face, lacks a coherent horizontal plane, or does not provide bowl-footprint margin.

entries.title: Resolve front and middle among identical bowls
fields: Distinguish the front and middle bowls using their current relative order. Preserve those identities when composing the requested stacking relation.
The task distinguishes front and middle bowls for a stacking relation.

Supporting observation: three distinct full masks whose row order is stable and whose public-depth geometry is bowl-like. Disconfirming observation: fewer than three distinct masks, a viewpoint where image row does not track table depth, or inconsistent depth ordering.

entries.title: Resolve the middle of three visible bowls
fields: When three distinct bowls have a clear horizontal order, bind the middle bowl by that order. Overlapping regions, a different count or an ambiguous relation make the rule inapplicable.
When three distinct bowls have a clear horizontal order.

Continue only while all three masks pass relative bowl geometry and deduplication checks. Call the method into question when there are not exactly three clean instances, X intervals overlap, occlusion makes centers unreliable, or public scene geometry indicates that 'middle' lies on another axis.

entries.title: Resolve the stove's actionable control
fields: Bind the stove's actionable control through its relationship to the stove, keeping cookware and unrelated neighboring parts separate.
The instruction is 'turn on the stove' and the scene contains a stove burner plus one raised rotary control amid unrelated cookware and handles.

Do not use generic 'object', 'switch', 'button', or 'handle' as the primary target. Disconfirming observation: a mask on another object, missing raised-control geometry, or failure of the selected feature to co-move on the first small action calls the binding into question and should stop the suffix. This is whole-program evidence without a matched referent ablation.

entries.title: Resolve tomato sauce among groceries
fields: For tomato-sauce placement, distinguish the upright can from ketchup bottles and other grocery packages before binding pickup.

For this task, when the public instruction says tomato sauce and the RGB contains a ketchup bottle, multiple cans, and other packages, test the observed class-qualified wording 'can of tomato sauce' before binding the pick sequence.

entries.title: Rotate while maintaining contact
fields: For a rotary control, advance contact position and orientation together around the visible pivot. Stop at the observed goal state instead of continuing an arbitrary larger turn.
Stove/oven knobs, appliance dials, valve handles, and similar vertical-axis controls.

Localize the semantic parent and raised actionable feature from public RGB/depth. Estimate the pivot from the broader lower body, preserve the grasp-minus-pivot offset, and advance both contact XY and tool orientation together in small angular increments.

entries.title: Select a grasp branch with transport clearance
fields: Choose an acquisition orientation with the later transport corridor in mind. A locally accessible contact may still obstruct the carried object on its route.
Bottles, cans, jars, and compact cylindrical packages moved into drawers, bins, shelves, or bounded surfaces.

Acquire with the verified sign, lift above surrounding geometry, then roll the retained object about the unchanged approach axis through short world-frame jaw-axis steps until reaching the equivalent opposite representation.

entries.title: Select body contact for an open vessel
fields: For an open vessel, choose a visible body or rim region that offers opposing solid surfaces and a clear approach.
Mugs, cups, handled cookware, and handled containers when a distinct handle is publicly visible.
Failure signature: top-down rim or nominal body grasps on an open vessel put a finger inside the opening, tip the vessel during close, or lose it on the first short lift.

entries.title: Select contact on a tall vessel
fields: For a tall vessel, select contact on its observed body with clearance for the approach and lift. Avoid treating the topmost visible point as the entire graspable region.
Pots, bottles, and lidded vessels in both object-on-surface and object-in-container tasks when a centered top feature is visible.

Repair: segment the whole object, use a robust extreme-top slice only to estimate body XY, keep an explicit world-frame jaw axis and downward approach selected from the public image, and take grasp Z from a side-contact band. If the broad low band is not reachable with open-finger clearance, switch to a narrower upper-body band without changing axes or target logic.

entries.title: Select the foreground support surface
fields: When foreground furniture and a rear counter compete as destinations, use their visible parent relationships and relative image positions to identify the intended support.
Object-on-cabinet, object-on-shelf, and object-on-appliance tasks with multiple visible horizontal surfaces.
Use robust planar-bound midpoints for target XY and the dense Z median for support height.

entries.title: Select the intended cabinet top
fields: Bind the intended foreground cabinet top using its visible position and supporting surface. A rear counter is not interchangeable with that destination.
The intended cabinet top competes with a rear counter as a placement destination.

Disconfirming observation: no broad foreground candidate, a candidate outside the task-relevant foreground/left region, sparse depth, or geometry inconsistent with an elevated support should leave the destination unresolved rather than force this rule.

entries.title: Select the requested cabinet and drawer
fields: Bind the requested cabinet and its specified drawer as a parent-part pair. Similar handles on another cabinet do not satisfy the instruction.
The instruction names a drawer belonging to a particular cabinet among similar visible handles.

Decision change: query the parent-qualified referent 'top drawer handle of the small cabinet', then accept it only when relative public image geometry and depth support the foreground small-cabinet handle (in the observed task view, a vertical handle box in the lower/foreground scene with sufficient valid depth) instead of taking the highest-score generic handle. Disconfirming observations: no parent-qualified mask, a horizontal/background candidate, insufficient depth, multiple context-valid candidates, or a differently oriented/occluded cabinet should stop selection and trigger re-observation rather than action.

entries.title: Select the task-qualified tomato-sauce can
fields: Use the task's tomato-sauce qualifier to distinguish the requested can from similar packages. Bind the source only when its visible identity and body geometry agree.
The requested tomato-sauce can must be separated from similar packages.
Proceed only when a compact upright can candidate has independent point-mask agreement. Reject the binding if those public observations disagree or no compact can is present.

entries.title: Separate a target from merged instances
fields: In clutter, reject a region that merges the requested object with its neighbors. Bind an isolated, shape-consistent instance before selecting its contact.
Cluttered cookware-to-appliance placement and handled-vessel-to-container/surface tasks.
In this task a pan-plus-moka union (240x133 px) outranked the clean moka (105x103 px).

entries.title: Separate contact from completed pickup
fields: For the cream-cheese package, distinguish initial contact from completed pickup. Preserve the task state until the requested package is supported as elevated with the hand.

This observation supports continuing the unexecuted carry suffix. If the requested package remains at source, execution of the frozen grasp is unsupported. If a different object moved, the target binding is wrong. If identity is ambiguous or occluded, stop unresolved while preserving the lifted scene and do not replay pickup.

entries.title: Separate gripper obstruction from retention
fields: A blocked gripper can reflect obstruction rather than acquisition of the bowl. Keep the held-state decision unresolved until the task object is supported as acquired.
After the selected white bowl rim is closed between the fingers, gripper aperture indicates obstruction but does not prove retention.
Stop without replay when identity or motion is not discriminating.

entries.title: Set release height relative to the support
fields: Ground a release in the current destination support. The hand's earlier height does not determine where the carried object's body should settle.
A placement predicate depends on stable support contact; gripper command completion alone is not physical release verification.

After opening, retract vertically along the reverse approach axis and request several observations for settling. Apply when a placement predicate depends on stable support contact. Gripper command completion alone is not physical release verification.

entries.title: Settle a handled vessel on its support
fields: For a handled vessel, observe its body and support during release. Finger contact can continue to support or disturb the vessel after the opening command.
Mugs, cups, bowls, and handled cookware placed on plates/trays/coasters or into broad containers.

From public depth, estimate the support center and trimmed planar half-extents, determine the handle-side direction from the public image or parent/handle masks, and shift the desired vessel-body landing point by a tested relative fraction of the support half-extent away from the handle while retaining margin inside the footprint. Preserve grasp-minus-body XY and the verified grasp/path.

entries.title: Stabilize a handled vessel
fields: For a handled open vessel that rotates during lift, choose engagement on a clear rim side and account for the handle's effect on the local contact.
Mugs, cups, bowls, and other open vessels.

Failure signature: an open vessel is retained by an exterior pinch but rotates during lift from handle or center-of-mass torque, or a shallow rim pinch closes successfully then slips late in transport. From public RGB/depth, select explicit world-frame closing and approach axes, estimate the rim from robust top points, shift the grasp center toward the exterior rim along the jaw axis so one finger is inside and one outside, and engage roughly 12-20 mm below the observed top when geometry permits.

entries.title: Stabilize contact on a compact package
fields: For a compact package, choose opposing body surfaces that can sustain the first lift. An initial close without stable body contact does not justify transport.
Cans/jars in container-placement tasks and cartons/boxes in surface or bin placement when center and contact height have already been checked.
Preserve the public-depth center, contact band, and world-down approach.

entries.title: Track the carried carton after transport
fields: After transporting a carton, track that same object's current relation to the destination. Preserve the completed carry while resolving the remaining placement objective.

Decision change: enumerate semantic candidates and select only one with enough public-depth points above basket-rim height and XY continuity with the completed high carry endpoint. Abort the suffix if none qualifies, then use only a bounded target-minus-held-body residual at high clearance. Disconfirming observation: no elevated endpoint-consistent candidate, an implausibly large residual, or public evidence that the carton was lost.

entries.title: Verify separation after opening the gripper
fields: After opening the gripper, inspect whether the object has separated from the fingers and settled on its support. Completion of the opening command alone does not establish release.

After opening at a small safe drop gap, retract vertically along the reverse approach direction to the clear transit pose, then allow settling. Treat gripper command completion as an actuator event, not proof of physical release.
